mars-station.header:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, intrigue. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- intrigue: Secrets, leverage and divided loyalties; people say less than they know.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Quiet, grounded hard SF; tension comes from secrets and pressure more than action.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom)
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons)
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons)
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons)
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons)
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons)
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface)
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface)
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

=== ESTABLISHED FACTS (known to the player) ===
- [T0] The recycler's rattle started six nights ago, the same night Teo had the late hydroponics shift.
- [T0] An orbital weather relay shows a regional dust storm building east of Hellas and tracking toward Ares Deep, roughly twenty hours out.
mars-station.intent:
=== NOW: Sol 214, 07:00 ===
Kit Navarro is in Commons.
World: power: solar arrays nominal; comms: online, 14-minute delay; recycler: degraded, about 70% output; rover: the Mule, operational
Pressures: Dust storm arrival 0/10; Water recycler failure 3/10
Groups: Mission Control: supportive but anxious; reviewing this rotation's data for the renewal decision; Halvorsen Aerospace: publicly upbeat; privately watching costs and crew performance
Present with Kit Navarro: Dr. Imani Okafor, Teo Bauer
Elsewhere: Dr. Lev Sorensen (Ops & Comms)

=== STATUS ===
- Kit Navarro (they/them) [navarro]: health unhurt; hunger low, fatigue low, stress moderate; feels toward: Dr. Imani Okafor neutral (10), Teo Bauer friendly (20)
- Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her) [okafor]: health unhurt; hunger low, fatigue moderate, stress moderate; feels toward Kit Navarro: neutral (10); toward others here: Teo Bauer neutral
- Teo Bauer (he/him) [bauer]: health unhurt; hunger low, fatigue moderate, stress high; feels toward Kit Navarro: friendly (20); toward others here: Dr. Imani Okafor neutral

=== PRIVATE (each item is known ONLY to the character named) ===
- Dr. Imani Okafor's secret: Three weeks ago she adjusted a core-sample report, overstating water-ice purity, because the real numbers might have ended the program. (guard: high; very hard to crack)
- Dr. Imani Okafor knows: Lev has been booking lab time far beyond his approved schedule.
- Teo Bauer's secret: He caused the recycler fault six nights ago by running it past its rated cycle to save a failing crop, then wiped that night's log. (guard: low; cracks easily when confronted)
- Teo Bauer knows: Hydroponics lost three racks of soy last week; he told the crew it was a lighting fault.

=== OFFSTAGE (not with the player; for events only) ===
- sorensen (Dr. Lev Sorensen), in Ops & Comms: wants be the first person to confirm life on Mars; secret: Cultures from the deep ice core are showing activity he cannot explain as contamination. He has told no one and keeps the samples in an unlogged incubator.

=== LAST SCENE ===
You look around. Nobody says much.

=== PLAYER ACTION (time passing: about an hour) ===
"Ask what happened."
The player's action takes up this whole span. Others act during the same span.

=== TASK ===
1. Judge the player's action. If it is risky, contested or depends on skill, set needs_roll to true and choose a skill (one of: tech, science, medicine, piloting, athletics, social, stealth) and a difficulty (easy, normal, hard). Talking, looking around and simple tasks need no roll. Everyone listed as present is in the same room as Kit Navarro right now, so an action about them needs no move. Only if the action clearly takes Kit Navarro somewhere else, set move_to to that location id (or to a character id to go where that character is).
2. You MUST give exactly one intent for EACH present character: okafor, bauer. Decide what each actually tries to do during this time, driven by their personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings. They may help, argue, refuse, lie, deflect, pursue their own goals, or leave (move_to). Set visible to false if they act covertly so the player would not notice.
3. "says": the gist of anything they say aloud this turn (or null).
4. "reveals": almost always null. Only fill it if the character deliberately says their secret or private knowledge out loud this turn, and that matches their "says". Being asked once, or being nervous, is not enough: people deflect, make excuses or lie first.
5. "events": things that happen during this span outside the player's control, to keep the world moving: offstage characters pursuing their wants and secrets, groups making moves that affect the people here, someone arriving, a call or message, something breaking down, the pressures above getting closer. How many: 0 or 1. Each event has:
   - "text": one sentence, with names.
   - "who": character ids involved (not the player).
   - "where": location id where it happens.
   - "visibility": "seen" (happens in the player's room), "heard" (the player gets a sound, call or message about it) or "hidden" (the player has no idea).
   - "moves": [{"id":"character_id","to":"location_id"}] for offstage characters who go somewhere because of it, else [].
   - "scope": "local" for these.
6. A REGIONAL event is due: add exactly one event with "scope":"regional" — something in the surroundings (terrain, weather, nearby places, infrastructure) that affects the people here. Ideas: dust devils crossing the solar field; an ice shelf collapsing near the drill site; a micrometeorite strike; a quake in the crater rim; the neighboring outpost going quiet on the regional relay; a supply drop landing off target; a rover track washed out by a slope failure.
   Give regional/world events concrete consequences in "effects":{"world":[{"key":"world_key","value":"new status"}],"groups":[{"id":"group_id","stance":"new stance"}],"clocks":[{"id":"clock_id","delta":2}],"new_clock":null}. Use only existing keys/ids (world keys: power, comms, recycler, rover; groups: mission, sponsor; clocks: storm, recycler). Use new_clock {"name":"short name","max":8,"perHour":0.2,"fireText":"what happens when it runs out"} only for a genuinely new looming problem. Usually "visibility":"heard" (news, a message, an alarm).
Reply with JSON only, exactly in this shape:
{"player":{"summary":"the player's action restated as a concrete attempt","needs_roll":false,"skill":null,"difficulty":"normal","move_to":null},
 "intents":[
  {"id":"okafor","action":"one sentence","says":null,"reveals":null,"visible":true,"needs_roll":false,"skill":null,"difficulty":"normal","move_to":null},
  {"id":"bauer","action":"one sentence","says":null,"reveals":null,"visible":true,"needs_roll":false,"skill":null,"difficulty":"normal","move_to":null}
 ],
 "events":[{"text":"one sentence","scope":"local","who":["character_id"],"where":"location_id","visibility":"heard","moves":[]}]}

Write the next scene in second person, present tense ("you" is Kit Navarro), 100–200 words. Bring the characters to life through dialogue and small actions in their own voices.
Time: This covers about an hour, all spent on the stated action. Play the key exchange as a live scene and compress the rest of the hour with a line or two ("For the next forty minutes…"). You may show how it naturally unfolds, but the player character starts no new activities and goes nowhere else. Their manner toward others matches the feelings listed in STATUS.
Beats: 2 or 3 beats. Start each beat on its own line with a time marker in brackets: minutes since the scene started, like [+0m], [+25m], [+50m] (use hours for long spans, like [+5h]). The last marker is at most [+60m]. Spread the beats across the whole span: the last one starts around [+45m]. End each beat on something the player could react to, since the player may step in between beats.
Structure:
1. The scene is set in Commons. Open with Kit Navarro's action, carried out in the first paragraph.
2. Then show how the others react to it and what they do, in the order that makes sense.
3. End on the others' latest move: a reply, a look, a question or a new problem the player can respond to. The final paragraph must NEVER be Kit Navarro's own line or action; leave Kit Navarro's response open for the player.
Hard rules:
- Narrate ONLY the resolved outcomes above, faithfully. Failures should cost something.
- Play Kit Navarro naturally, in character (voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.). If the action is vague, fill it in the way Kit Navarro would: small gestures, a line or two of dialogue, how they go about it.
- Do not make big choices for Kit Navarro: no agreeing to plans, making promises, starting new tasks, revealing what Kit Navarro knows beyond the action, or deciding what to do next. When a real choice comes up, stop there and leave it to the player.
- Kit Navarro never leaves Commons. Do not take Kit Navarro anywhere else.
- Only the characters in the frame appear. Anyone "out of your sight" is NOT seen doing it; at most a sound or a hint.
- Characters may leave or arrive when it fits the outcomes and events; anyone who leaves is seen leaving, not followed.
- EVENTs tagged [regional] or [world] reach the scene the way they realistically would (a tremor, an alarm, a message or news report), and the present characters react to them in character.
- Use each character's pronouns exactly as given in STATUS (e.g. he/him means "he", never "they").
- Characters reveal only what is listed under REVEALS. Anything else they keep to themselves: they deflect, stall, joke or lie.
- Do not invent new events, confessions or discoveries.
- Stop at the end of these outcomes, on a moment that invites the player's response. Do not continue past it.
Reply with the scene text only.

zombie-holdout.header:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Holdout at Harmon's ===
Day 23 of the outbreak. Five strangers have barricaded themselves inside Harmon's Hardware, a rural store off a two-lane highway. The town is quiet in the worst way. Radio and phones are mostly dead, gas is scarce, and the dead are slow but endless. Nobody here chose each other.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: survival, horror, grim. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- survival: Scarcity, exposure and exhaustion press on every choice; ordinary tasks take real effort.
- horror: Dread builds slowly; imply more than you show; quiet moments feel uneasy.
- grim: Hard choices without good options; kindness costs something, and losses stay lost.
A major event here means: a threat to the group's survival (supplies lost, shelter breached, someone badly hurt).
Danger is lethal. Injuries are serious and people can die.
Tone: Bleak and personal: the dead are constant pressure, the living are the drama.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Jordan Pike (id: pike). Never decide Jordan Pike's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- The dead are slow, relentless and drawn by noise and light. A bite is fatal within a day or two; there is no cure.
- Realistic tone: injuries matter, supplies run out, guns are loud and ammunition is scarce.
- The living are the real danger: fear, grudges and secrets drive conflict inside the group.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- floor: Sales Floor — Aisles of tools and paint, front windows boarded with plywood. (connects: stockroom, office, dock)
- stockroom: Stockroom — Shelving, bedrolls on cardboard and the group's food pile. (connects: floor, dock)
- office: Manager's Office — A locked desk, a dead landline and a ladder to the roof hatch. (connects: floor, roof)
- roof: Roof — Flat tar roof with a view of the highway and the town. (connects: office)
- dock: Loading Dock — Rolling steel door, a forklift and the only vehicle exit. (connects: floor, stockroom, lot)
- lot: Parking Lot — Open asphalt, abandoned cars, a pickup with no keys. Exposed. (connects: dock)

=== GROUPS ===
- convoy: Coastal rescue convoy — An armed convoy evacuating survivors to a coastal safe zone, broadcasting on handheld radio bands.
- ridge: The Ridge — Armed survivors holed up in the next town over. Nobody here knows much about them.

=== CAST ===
- pike (PLAYER): Jordan Pike (they/them), former delivery driver, 33. Traits: steady, observant, dry. Voice: Few words, dry humor, calm under pressure.
- ortiz: Marlene Ortiz (she/her), retired ER nurse, 58. Traits: practical, maternal, guilt-ridden. Wants: keep everyone fed and together, and never abandon anyone again. Voice: Calm and warm, calls people 'honey', goes cold when angry.
- coleman: Dex Coleman (he/him), army reservist, 26. Traits: brave, hotheaded, loyal to a fault. Wants: get to his sister's last known location in the next county. Voice: Loud, quick, military slang, jokes when scared.
- han: Ruth Han (she/her), auto mechanic, 29. Traits: quiet, calculating, self-reliant. Wants: get out of this town for good. Voice: Short sentences, long silences, rarely smiles.
- ferris: Gil Ferris (he/him), store owner, 61. Traits: territorial, paranoid, shrewd. Wants: keep control of his store and come out of this with something left. Voice: Gruff, folksy, reminds everyone whose store this is.

=== ESTABLISHED FACTS (known to the player) ===
- [T0] Gil Ferris keeps the office locked even at night and gets defensive when anyone goes near it.
- [T0] A large crowd of the dead was seen two miles up the highway yesterday, drifting slowly south toward the store.
